jp: 私[わたし]{なんか/など|nanka-nante}{が|ga-subject}先生[せんせい]{に|ni-change}なれるでしょう{か|ka-question}。
en: Could someone like me really become a teacher?
why: なんか humbly belittles the speaker: someone like me.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{なんか/など|nanka-nante}{に|ni-target}出[で]る時間[じかん]{は|wa-topic}ありません。
en: I have no time to attend things like meetings.
why: なんか treats meetings as unimportant, with a dismissive tone: things like meetings.

jp: 成績[せいせき]{なんか/など|nanka-nante}{を|o-object}自慢[じまん]し{ても|te-mo}、仕方[しかた]ありません。
en: It's no use bragging about something as trivial as grades.
why: なんか downplays grades as something petty to brag about.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{が|ga-subject}遅刻[ちこく]する{なんて|nanka-nante}、珍[めずら]しいです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: Mr. Tanaka being late? That's unusual, isn't it!
why: After a clause, なんて expresses surprise that something happened.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]{が|ga-subject}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}案[あん]{を|o-object}ほめてくれた{なんて|nanka-nante}、本当[ほんとう]にうれしいです。
en: I can hardly believe the manager praised my proposal; I'm really happy.
why: なんて after a clause voices surprise that the unexpected thing happened.
